evidence: PDF pp.3–8 Figures 1–3, Table 1, Algorithm 1: L1 reference-free heuristics, L2 reference-dependent transport and L3 schema-dependent irreversible-action gate; online artifact-string extraction can miss semantic/shell-resolved dependencies. Generated reference skeletons cannot authorize automatic halts.

PDF pp.5–9 Eqs.2–10 and Proposition 1: fixed node mass, frontier masking, one warm-start CG step and escalation; implementation clips the GW gradient and reports an L1 mass surrogate. Final equality requires matching online/batch graphs and identical cold-start solver inputs, not exact minimization or global optimality. The .013 discrepancy is against eventual finalization, not same-prefix tracking error.

PDF pp.9–10 Tables 2–3: eight designed scenarios pass; a prior stale-frontier bug blocked 50/50 valid calls, then 0/50 after repair (95% upper bound about 6%). SWE-agent has no irreversible-annotated tools, so L3 does not run there. No-schema/no-reference policy is allow-by-default, not a safety guarantee.

PDF p.10 Table 4: full system hallucination/inversion detection 12/30 each with 13/40 benign traces flagged; no-GW 21/30 and 25/30 with 29/40 flagged. No-mask changes benign count only to 14/40. Released-sweep claims put hallucination/inversion AUPRC .44–.47 near .45 base rate for all variants, so the lower false-alarm point is not curve-level dominance.

PDF p.11 Section 6.2: 2,294 traces, 2,288 usable (430 resolved/1,858 unresolved), six malformed excluded; 228 calibration instances, five reference instances, remaining evaluation, seed42; one trace per instance. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and calibration-selected lambda=.3 are frozen.

PDF p.11 Table 5: at k=8 OnTrack .631 versus cosine .574, difference .057 [95% CI .033,.080]; by k=15 difference .002 [-.022,.027]. LinUOT is .628 at k=8. Reviewer inference: n_steps AUROC .622 at k=5 cannot arise from a constant five-step prefix count under the stated fixed-k protocol; use of another length variable or full future length needs clarification, not an assumption of verified online availability.

PDF p.12 Table 6: threshold .60 gives 23.3% unresolved stops, 20.7% resolved false stops and author-reported 17.9% failed-population cost savings on 150+150 profiles. Precision83% is adjusted to an81%-unresolved corpus. Threshold .60 is explicitly selected for exposition after the sweep; fixed-FPR rates are evaluation ROC readouts, not pre-registered deployment thresholds. Rival cutoffs match or exceed savings at some matched false-stop rates.

PDF pp.12–13: authors explicitly state the data log only per-trace, not per-step cost, and remaining-step fraction does not license dollar conversion; a precise cost allocation for Table6 is not supplied. Thus savings are an author-reported replay estimate, not directly measured intervention-time billing savings. Median detection at58.6% of cost-limit trace steps is not58.6% of dollars.

PDF pp.13–14 Tables7–8: cost-limit AUROC .979 matches step count .978; real three-step splice score AUROC .546 and leakage p=.93; length-matched outcome AUROC .526 versus cosine .540. Controlled hallucination success does not transfer to general real-trace semantic error detection.

PDF pp.15–16 AppendixA/Table9: five seeds resample evaluation traces with partition, references and lambda fixed. Reviewer inference: class prevalence alone does not systematically alter AUROC, so the table caption's attribution of higher AUROC to class balancing is not generally valid; finite-sample selection can vary estimates. These are not five independent training or split replications.

PDF pp.9–10: fast-path p50 .85ms/p95 1.6ms at t=m40,K3 on an Apple M5 Max core; escalated solve approximately30ms, and no demonstrated long-horizon compression. End-to-end embedding/extraction overhead is not separately characterized.

Complete PDF pp.1–16 and retained official abs.html: full methods, references and AppendixA present; external code/config/result JSON release is claimed without a concrete repository link identified in the inspected source. No external artifact or author code was executed.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly relevant engineering research with useful architectural separation and unusually explicit negative findings. The most defensible result is an early alignment advantage over cosine on replayed SWE-agent traces, not superior general hallucination detection or safe autonomous stopping. GW mainly changes the shipped operating point; matched PR curves and ranking do not establish dominance. Prefix-fixed step-count discrimination is an unresolved protocol inconsistency, and the corpus has no per-step costs, so claimed compute savings require an accounting assumption that is not adequately specified. A 20.7% successful-run false-stop rate and post-hoc threshold selection materially limit deployment value despite the failure-skewed precision. Batch reduction is to the same implemented clipped-gradient/surrogate solver with identical initialization, not an exact OT optimum or a per-prefix tracking theorem. Complete PDF access supports this bounded assessment; external release and experiment replication were not performed.

primary_link.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport

papers.summary: Agents are deployed in applications from trip planners and stock trading to IT incident triage. In most cases, LLM agents work autonomously with minimal rule-based safeguarding, leading to cost and safety issues from irreversible actions. Recent works resolve this either by using a safeguard agent to monitor behavior or evaluating logs post-hoc. The first adds cost and latency to every step; the second delivers its verdict after the run, when tokens are burned and damage is done. To overcome this, we propose OnTrack, a streaming monitoring mechanism that compares an agent's steps and dependencies against recorded successful runs to alert users or block the agent in about a millisecond per step. We study this problem in three regimes of decreasing access: full reference access (historical runs and tool schemas), intermediate access (only tool schemas), and no prior knowledge (only step logs as generated). Expectation of OnTrack's monitoring capabilities reduces as data access drops, ranging from plan violation detection to identifying loops, stalls, and repeated tool calls. Finally, we evaluate OnTrack using SWE-bench trajectories. Based on the first 8 steps, our method ranks failing trajectories below succeeding ones better than content similarity approaches (+0.057 AUROC). With an abort policy, we save about 18% of compute that would be burned on failing runs, where 83% of interrupted runs were actually heading to failure (5 out of 6 aborts were correct).
papers.summary_en: OnTrack aligns growing dependency graphs with successful references, combining transport signals with loop heuristics and schema gates. At eight SWE-agent steps it reports AUROC .631 versus cosine .574, but structure adds little ranking value and gains vanish later. The illustrative abort policy saves about 18% on failed runs while stopping about 21% of successes; its 83% precision relies on an 81% failure base rate. Prefix-length and cost-accounting ambiguities, weak real anomaly detection and unverified code limit deployment claims.
papers.summary_zh:
代理在執行中繞圈或偏離計畫時，等整段日誌結束才評分往往太晚。OnTrack 把逐步事件建成相依圖，將已發生的前綴與成功參考軌跡對齊；以可執行前緣遮罩避免處罰尚未做到的步驟，並用暖啟動求解與短暫探索寬限處理延後才出現的依賴。循環與停滯由無參考啟發式偵測，不可逆工具的阻擋則依賴明示工具契約，兩者不能全部歸功於最佳傳輸。

作者重播二千二百八十八條可解析 SWE-agent 軌跡，在前八步得到 AUROC 0.631，比餘弦相似度高 0.057；十五步後差距消失，拿掉結構項也幾乎不改排名。停止策略報告可省失敗群體約十八％成本，但同一設定會誤停約二十一％原本成功的軌跡；八十三％停止精確率依賴語料本就有八十一％失敗，不能讀成高可靠度防護。

完整十六頁、三圖與九表顯示，這較適合作為低延遲流程告警的工程提案。真實軌跡中的幻覺與因果顛倒接近偵測下限，安全閘門未在這批真實工具上觸發。另須留意：固定前綴長度下，步數基線卻有非隨機辨識率，資訊來源未交代；逐步成本也未記錄，節省數字不能當成已量測的帳單節省。停止門檻為事後示例，尚需獨立校準與效用評估；程式釋出聲稱本次未另行驗證。

links.title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents

evidence: PDF pp.6–8, Sections 3.2–3.5 and Figure 2: 20,947 repository snapshots, 5,106 reconstructed installation lists, 43,986 installed-skill families; 439,860 cross-project plus 382,249 within-project candidate pairs. Only the most similar above-floor candidate per sampling unit is judged in the main stratified sample; 1,639 of 3,754 pairs are confirmed.

PDF pp.8–9, Sections 3.6–3.7 and Table 2: core functions are extracted from each skill before runs, quoted/checkable/skill-specific, ranked, with the first three applicable treated as primary. 73% of 2,518 applicable experimental requirements are exclusive to A; 312 selected pairs must be retrievable and offline runnable, and cases are LLM-drafted with at most 15 repository files.

PDF pp.9–12, Table 3 and Sections 3.8–3.10: A-only, B-only, A+B, unrelated A+C, swapped and scope conditions; 5,162 analyzed main runs of 5,166 planned, plus 670 guard and 536 extra repeat runs total 6,368. One main sample per pair/model/configuration; repeated-combination agreement and ICC do not eliminate sampling variability.

PDF pp.10–11, Section 3.8: Claude Code 2.1.283, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 and Opus 5; 80-turn/25-minute limits. Skill-list budget raised to 20,000 characters because 95.8% of default Opus A+B listings would truncate a description. This is an explicit experimental deviation from normal defaults.

PDF pp.11–12, Sections 3.9–3.10: 327 of 921 primary checks are scripts, 594 use GPT-6 Astra; most task completion also uses this judge with masked names/paths. Human-consensus versus LLM alpha is .78 for core-function verdicts, .75 for task completion, .72 for pair confirmation and .74 for exclusive/shared labels, so validation is informative but imperfect.

PDF pp.12–14, Section 4.1 and Figure 4: estimated same-job overlap is 23.5% within reconstructed lists and 63.7% across authors, restricted to the sampled frames. A-only primary fidelity is 57.3%, B-only 46.3%. A+B lowers A use by 19.9pp [−23.1,−16.7], primary fidelity by 2.6pp [−4.4,−0.8], and all applicable exclusive fidelity by 5.6pp [−7.3,−3.8]. Task completion +1.9pp [−1.0,+4.9] is no detected reduction, not established equivalence.

PDF pp.13–14, Figure 4 and sensitivity analysis: unrelated C lowers A use by 5.9pp and primary fidelity by .2pp; A+B's loss remains on script-decided functions at 4.2pp [−7.6,−.9]. Substitution/interference groups condition on post-treatment skill use and are descriptive decomposition, not randomized mechanism assignments.

PDF pp.14–15, Figure 5: order effect on A use +.6pp [−2.0,+3.3] is distinguished from a +4.4pp naming effect. Same-name personal B removes A from all 243 listings, yet A files are still read in 29.2% of runs. Only .9% of 113 substituted runs name the used skill in the final reply; this metric does not measure all possible UI disclosure.

PDF pp.15–16, Figure 6 and Section 4.4: 79 pair/model combinations changing first-opened skill yield exclusive-fidelity difference −9.4pp [−15.0,−4.0]; first-read order was observed, not randomly assigned. 97% of B-first runs had not changed files before that read, not evidence that no other side effects occurred.

PDF pp.12 and 16, guard experiment: 187 at-risk pair/model combinations (119 pairs), randomized guarded/unguarded reruns, 670 runs. Guard blocks B while A is unread and after A is in use; it knows A's identity. 96% of 179 first-reach denials redirect to A; exclusive fidelity gains 9.1pp [6.0,12.1] over all runs. Redirected-versus-A-first difference 0pp [−10.2,+10.3] does not establish complete equivalence; task-completion +4.1pp [−1.3,+9.6] is likewise inconclusive for equivalence.

PDF pp.6 and 17: Codex check on 193 pairs/three OpenAI models reports A-use decline 18.2pp and first-three-exclusive fidelity decline 3.4pp, versus Claude 20.1pp/4.6pp on those same pairs. These differ in sample and requirement definition from the full-set 19.9pp/5.6pp and should not be conflated; the PDF supplies limited replication detail for this check.

PDF pp.19–22: data-availability statement links https://github.com/ltroin/conflict and claims cases, prompts, identifiers, annotations, harness, 6,368 logs and analysis scripts, with license-limited skill contents. This repository was not fetched or executed in this review; no missing in-file appendix is cited.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A strong, highly relevant measurement study showing why task completion can miss loss of user-specific skill requirements. Its paired original/similar/unrelated conditions, frozen requirement checks, sampled human validation and hook intervention provide substantially more evidence than a retrieval-only benchmark. The central losses are modest in overall fidelity but larger for exclusive requirements, and should not be conflated with a one-in-five task failure rate. The guard assumes the intended skill is already known; first-read ordering is partly observational, and confidence intervals crossing zero do not prove unchanged task success or complete restoration. Generated offline tasks, a raised listing budget, one main sample per cell and a common construction/judging model bound deployment relevance. All 22 PDF pages and six figures/three tables were read; the replication repository was not independently validated.

The guard assumes the intended skill is already known; first-read ordering is partly observational, and confidence intervals crossing zero do not prove unchanged task success or complete restoration. llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是一項高度相關且設計完整的測量研究，說明任務成功仍可能漏掉使用者特定技能要求。原技能、相似技能與不相關技能的配對對照、事前固定檢查、人工抽查與護欄介入，比只評估檢索命中更有證據。整體遵循下降較小，獨有要求下降較大，不能把使用率減少誤寫為五分之一任務失敗。護欄假設正確技能已知，首讀順序部分來自觀察，區間跨零也不證明任務成功等效或規範完全恢復。生成離線任務、提高列表容量、各條件主要只有一次執行，以及共用建構與裁判模型，都限制部署推論。二十二頁、六圖與三表已完整閱讀，重現套件未獨立驗證。

primary_link.title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents

top5.summary: Coding agents are extended with agent skills, directories whose SKILL.md tells the model when and how to perform a task. Because skills come from independent sources (teams, developers, plugins, copied collections), an installed skill can be co-installed with a similar skill doing the same job, and the model picks between them by name and description alone. In a conflict, the installed skill loses core functions (e.g., a ban on touching git) because the similar skill runs instead or changes what it does. The task still passes, so benchmarks that check only task completion miss such cases. We present the first empirical study of such conflicts. From snapshots of 20,947 repositories, we mine 822,109 candidate similar-skill pairs, have an LLM judge a stratified sample of 3,754, and run 312 confirmed pairs on three models (6,368 runs, 169,294 tool calls, 542 agent-hours). We report five findings. (1) Conflict-prone skills are common: nearly one in four installed skills is co-installed with one that does the same job, and 37% of judged skills sit inside copied collections. (2) Most such pairs involve normative skills, then capability skills. (3) Without lowering task completion, a similar skill takes one in five runs from the installed skill, and runs that open the similar skill first lose over a third of the exclusive core functions that only the installed skill fulfills. (4) Install location decides which skill runs, listing order barely matters, and the final reply names the skill used in only 0.9% of substituted runs. (5) Conflicts are decided at the first skill read, almost always before any file is changed, and a pre-tool hook at that read restores fidelity on exclusive core functions to the level of runs that open the installed skill first. Benchmarks should thus score exclusive core functions, and platforms should guard the first read and show which skill ran.
top5.summary_en: Co-installed skills can preserve task success while eroding the conventions a user expected. Across 312 skill pairs, a similar skill reduced use of the original by 19.9 percentage points and fidelity to its exclusive requirements by 5.6 points. An unrelated-skill control and a first-read hook strengthen the case. Yet the hook already knows which skill should win; synthetic offline tasks, shared LLM judging and enlarged listing limits constrain transfer. Null differences do not establish equivalence.
top5.summary_zh:
任務完成，並不表示代理遵守了你安裝技能時要求的流程。這篇研究把技能的獨有規範拆成可檢查的核心功能，觀察兩個能做同類工作的技能共同安裝後，原技能是否被替代，以及禁止提交、指定格式等要求是否流失。作者從公開程式庫建立安裝清單，抽樣判定功能重疊，再以三個 Claude 模型測試三百一十二組技能，另提供 Codex 的有限跨平台比較。

主要配對實驗中，加入相似技能使原技能使用率下降 19.9 個百分點，獨有核心功能的滿足率下降 5.6 點；加入不相關技能的影響較小。任務完成率沒有顯著下降，但這不是等效或無害證明。研究也發現，替代行為很少在最終回覆揭露；多數先讀相似技能的執行在首次讀取前尚未改檔，適合設置攔截點。

首次讀取護欄能改善規範遵循，但它事先知道應優先使用哪個技能，尚未解決自動識別衝突與判定使用者意圖。實驗還提高技能列表容量，案例由模型生成且限離線小型程式庫，多數條件只跑一次；人工核對與腳本負控提升可信度，仍不能消除共用模型裁判的偏差。全文及圖表已核對，公開套件未重跑；價值在於把任務成功與規範遵循分開評估，而非證明護欄可以保證安全。

links.title: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models

evidence: Main PDF pp.1–5, Table 1 and footnote 2: omission rates 45.60% (DeepSeek) and 56.92% (GLM), versus forbidden-action 33.52%/30.00%, are percentages of evaluated executions restricted to those passing functional tests. Labels can overlap. These are not all-task or deployment prevalence estimates; the PDF does not report underlying preliminary counts.

Main PDF pp.6–8, Figures 3–4: 240 instances = 120 positive/120 matched negatives, 339 obligations; domains 80 issue resolution/32 feature development/128 terminal. Positive set sizes 24×1+21×2+36×3+30×4+9×5 sum to 339. Source pool: 1,000 tasks/four backends/5,684 valid trajectories; repeated rollout allocation is not fully specified. GPT-5.6-Sol screens and annotates; negatives are rerun until empty; 360 candidates become 240 after two-engineer review (82.2% pre-adjudication set agreement) and ambiguity removal.

Main PDF pp.8–11 and Supplement p.1: scenario planning produces 10,000 templates, trajectory synthesis produces 40,000 training examples; full-parameter Qwen3-8B SFT uses two epochs, AdamW 1e−5, effective batch32 and max32,768 tokens. Supplement adds 2,000 validation examples, eight A100-80GB, BF16/ZeRO-3, 5% warmup/cosine decay and best validation-EM checkpoint selection. Independent checking that every planned label matches each synthetic trajectory is not demonstrated.

Main PDF pp.10–12, Equations 6–9 and Table 2: micro precision/recall and exact set match are positive-only; CA+ only requires any nonempty prediction, not a correct obligation, and CA− requires empty output. ObligationGuard has precision82.98, recall57.52, EM21.67, CA+85.83, CA−89.17. Recall corresponds to 195/339 gold obligations and EM26/120 sets; negative CA implies 13/120 false-positive cases.

Main PDF p.12 Table 2: strongest pre-existing recall48.97 is Claude-Opus-4.8, whose EM is9.17; strongest pre-existing EM10.00 is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The distinct maxima must not be attributed to a single model. Qwen3-8B baseline recall15.34/EM.83; main 8B gain does not mean it exceeds the authors' larger14B ablation (recall62.54/EM25.83, p.14).

Main PDF pp.12–13 Figure 6: longer earliest-obligation-to-termination distance and more obligations correlate with lower recall/EM averaged over five models. These are stratified observations without randomized distance/count intervention or uncertainty bars; task difficulty, domain and trajectory length can confound mechanism claims.

Main PDF pp.14–15, Table 3/Figures 7–8: gains extend to4B/14B Qwen and8B Llama. 5K→40K improves8B recall32.45→57.52 and EM5.00→21.67. Direct synthesis at40K yields recall45.43/EM8.33 versus planned-template57.52/21.67. Equal example count and optimizer do not establish equal data-generation compute or repeated-training robustness.

Main PDF pp.15–17, Tables 4–5/Figure 9: Qwen3.8-27B on186 SusVibes tasks receives one intervention at first attempted termination, with shared initial state. Safe-pass12/186≈6.5% becomes28/186≈15.1%; functional-pass51/186≈27.4% becomes50/186≈26.9%. Transition table shows16 initially correct-unsafe become safe, one incorrect becomes safe, three correct-unsafe become incorrect and one previously safe becomes unsafe. Gains do not erase regressions.

Main PDF pp.16–17: recall versus downstream safe-pass improvement has Spearman .94/Pearson .97 over six guard sources. This tiny model-level association is not causal proof that increasing recall alone guarantees better safety; precision and feedback behavior also vary.

Main PDF p.17 Section7.1 and Supplement pp.16–17: semantic matching uses maximum one-to-one matches, hides evaluated model identity and temperature0. Human checking confirms196/200 matches and184/200 nonmatches (95% balanced-sample agreement). This validates sampled pair judgments, not completeness of all benchmark obligation sets or deployment-weighted error rates.

Supplement pp.2–22, Table1/Figures1–11: full prompts for identification, failure attribution, filtering, annotation, scenario planning, synthesis, semantic matching, creation-step annotation, direct synthesis, self-reminder and feedback are available and were read. Identification requires a necessary executed action creating the obligation and concrete safety consequence; prompts are evidence, not instructions executed by this reviewer.

Supplement pp.23–28, Figures12–16: five fully read case figures illustrate missing audit finalization, retained plaintext, stale authorization/streams, confusion between removed and still-authorized accounts, and retained CA trust/key. The supplement explicitly says the displayed trajectories omit input and some model evidence fields; these are illustrative excerpts, not the full240-record dataset.

Official repository README at commit58f644a25e801cb19dca961ba6df0b354c640551 states complete240 instances at data/obligationbench.jsonl, trajectory-level split seed4258302180, and configurations/revisions in configs/. It also states malformed/incomplete identification output is scored as empty. llm_evaluation.rationale: A relevant benchmark and training study that makes safety-critical omissions explicit rather than assuming action-level permission is sufficient. Matched negatives, human correction, multiple ablations, full supplementary prompts and an end-to-end shared-state experiment substantiate the idea. The quantitative claims require careful denominators: preliminary omission prevalence is conditional on functionally passing executions; precision/recall/exact match concern positive cases, whereas false alarms are separate. The reported downstream increase is 12 to 28 safe completions out of 186, with regressions, not guaranteed safety. One-run evaluation without intervals, curation and shared-model bias, possible output-schema penalties for specialized guards, and non-inspection of full datasets prevent a stronger reliability claim. The complete main PDF plus official supplement is sufficient for this bounded source-based review; unverified data and reproduction limit specific validation claims rather than requiring a blanket missing-source hold.

primary_link.title: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models

top5.summary: Guard models are increasingly used to safeguard LLM-based agents, primarily by identifying actions that agents are forbidden to perform. However, identifying forbidden actions alone is insufficient to ensure agent safety. In this paper, we argue that agent safety also depends on identifying required yet unperformed safety-critical actions, which we call obligations. Our preliminary study on a popular benchmark for evaluating safety shows that 56.92% of GLM-5.3 trajectories contain unfulfilled obligations, compared with only 30.00% containing forbidden actions. This finding reveals unfulfilled obligations as a major and previously overlooked source of safety risk. However, to our knowledge, no existing benchmark evaluates whether guard models can identify these obligations. To close this gap, we introduce ObligationBench, the first benchmark for evaluating the capability of obligation identification, comprising 240 expert-validated trajectories covering issue resolution, feature development, and terminal operations. Our evaluation of 14 representative models reveals substantial limitations: the highest recall and exact-match rate are only 48.97% and 10.00%, respectively. To address these limitations, we develop ObligationGuard using 40,000 synthetic training examples. ObligationGuard achieves 57.52% recall and an exact-match rate of 21.67%, surpassing all evaluated models on both metrics. We call on the community to incorporate obligation identification into the design and evaluation of future guard models to improve agent safety.
top5.summary_en: ObligationBench tests safety-critical actions an agent omitted, using 120 positive and 120 negative trajectories. Synthetic training gives an 8B guard 57.52% recall and 21.67% exact set match. On 186 SusVibes tasks, safe functional completions rise from 12 to 28, with some regressions. The idea is useful, but curated cases, single runs, shared LLM judging and output-format effects limit the evidence. The 21-page paper and 28-page supplement were read; full datasets and executions were not reproduced.
top5.summary_zh:
沒有做出禁止動作，仍可能留下安全風險：例如完成維護後未撤回臨時權限，或測試結束後保留敏感檔案。這篇研究把這些應做卻未做的安全動作稱為「義務」，提出 ObligationBench，從程式修復、功能開發與終端任務蒐集軌跡，整理成各一百二十例的正負案例，由兩位工程師核對標註。這是刻意篩選的測試集，不能用其比例推算部署中的風險盛行率。

作者先規劃應留下哪些義務，再生成軌跡，以四萬筆資料微調八十億參數模型。在主要比較中，ObligationGuard 的召回率為 57.52%，完整找對整組義務的比例為 21.67%；它仍漏掉不少義務。接入代理後，一百八十六項 SusVibes 任務中，同時通過功能與安全測試的案例由十二個增至二十八個，但也有少數原本成功的案例退步，不能只用「提升兩倍」概括成安全保證。

研究的價值在於補上終止前的安全收尾檢查，並用相同執行狀態比較提醒與具體義務回饋。限制包括單次評估、缺少誤差區間、共用生成與裁判模型，以及一般防護模型可能不適應輸出格式。二十一頁主文與二十八頁官方補充已讀，訓練設定和完整提示詞已補齊；五個案例只有軌跡摘錄，完整資料與程式未重跑，數字應視為作者報告的有界證據。

To avoid similarity with Product Manager, non-coder goal stability is changed from the highest-multiplier stable choice to pivoting. Previously unsolved covered subtasks later have at least one architect-condition success. Nodes failing or uncollectable on final reference state are excluded; P2P failing on the base-plus-seed state is reassigned to F2P.

PDF pp.24–25, Appendix B.1: assistant temperature 0, generation cap 32,768, 250 shell steps per user turn, turn cap three times subtask count. Simulator fixed GLM-5.2, confidence-driven early termination and hidden-test feedback vary by persona; common maxima do not equalize realized computation. Cost/Session excludes simulator tokens.

PDF pp.25–26/Table 10: only eleven open-model rows have single-shot comparisons; the runner allows 2,000 total steps. Mean final F2P is 60.31% single-shot versus 75.94% architect interaction. This is not a controlled equal-compute attribution of the benefit to interaction alone.

PDF pp.26–27, Appendix B.3: reported manual checks sample 50 instances per metric with over 90% accuracy; no detailed annotator agreement is supplied. Miss excludes no-locus turns from its denominator despite abbreviated all-turn wording elsewhere. Fix requires emitted reasoning, so two proprietary models are unmeasured, not zero.

PDF pp.18–19, Table 5: environment setup and repository collaboration each show 3.3%, whereas the following prose calls those the two absent categories. Documentation and external integration are actually 0.0% in the displayed table. Figure 3 on p.22 annotates 3.83 task angles while pp.18/23 say 3.80. These are reporting inconsistencies, not missing PDF pages.

PDF pp.22–24/Figures 3–4: coverage and realism come from model-assigned categories or 1–5 judgments, with no real-user intervention study. Thirty synthesized cases and the synthetic-user scoring loop limit external validity; main tables lack repeated-run confidence intervals.

PDF pp.31–32/Tables 20–21 and pp.43–45/C.5: retrieval exposure is observed rather than randomized. GPT seed F2P 76.76% versus synthetic 47.54% compares different task provenance/difficulty. Matching module hashes in R1 demonstrate seed reuse; R2 shows upstream reference use still requiring new interfaces. Neither establishes that all synthetic tasks are contamination-free.

PDF pp.33–45, Appendix C: selected transcripts illustrate clarification, misleading steering, self-confirming tests, confidence/correctness mismatch and answer retrieval. A single illustrative complete user/reply sequence appears in C.1 with marked reply elisions, despite an earlier statement promising two; raw full trajectories and complete tools are not supplied in the PDF.

llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant evaluation design that exposes how coding performance depends on ongoing requirement discovery, state retention and verification. The 78.50% versus 23.00% final F2P contrast is compelling within the four simulated collaboration conditions, but is not a real-user success rate or an isolated expertise effect. Non-coder pivoting is deliberately imposed, the source subgroup has 27 logs, realized compute differs and no main-result uncertainty is shown. Solvability checks and test normalization are useful; model-judged realism, observational retrieval comparisons, limited release verification and minor coverage-reporting conflicts keep the overall assessment calibrated.

primary_link.title: SWE-Journey: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Coding Assistants through Long-Horizon, Multi-Turn Interaction

top5.summary: Coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex have become a major application of LLM agents, yet existing benchmarks remain far from real-world use, particularly in task horizon and interaction length. Code assistants require completing long chains of development work in continuously evolving repositories, while repeatedly clarifying requirements and adapting implementations through multi-turn interaction. To address these gaps, we introduce SWE-Journey, a benchmark for more realistic evaluation of coding assistants. To address the task-horizon gap, we propose a weak-to-strong synthesis pipeline that automatically constructs long-horizon coding tasks. To address the interaction gap, we mine four representative user personas from real interaction data and build a user-simulation agent to reproduce realistic code-assistance interactions. On average, models pass over 75% of tests for requested functionality with software architects, but fewer than 25% with non-coders. These results show that current coding assistants still fall short of enabling reliable coding for non-coders. We further analyze the reasons for this gap and identify asking right, finding right, and fixing right as key capabilities during interaction.
top5.summary_en: SWE-Journey evaluates 30 long-horizon coding tasks with four simulated user profiles. Across 13 models, final feature-test pass rates average 78.50% with architects and 23.00% with non-coders. These are test-node rates under bundled collaboration conditions, not project success or a causal expertise effect. Read the persona design and test reclassification before the rankings: compute varies, realism is model-judged, and main-result uncertainty is absent. All 45 pages, four figures and 21 tables were read.
top5.summary_zh:
單次修好程式，不等於能陪使用者完成持續演變的開發工作。SWE-Journey 用較強模型規劃、較弱模型逐步生成修補與測試，串成三階段任務，再由固定使用者模擬器扮演四種角色，與程式代理共用持續保留狀態的容器。三十個案例涵蓋五百九十四項子任務；評估分開量測新功能測試通過率與既有功能保留率，亦比較使用者以為完成時和最終交付時的程式。

十三模型的結果顯示，模擬軟體架構師條件下平均最終新功能通過率為 78.50%，Non-coder 條件則為 23.00%。這是測試節點比例，不是整個專案完成率。差距也不能歸因於專業程度一項：角色同時改變資訊、需求穩定性與驗證方式，非程式使用者的反覆改向是作者刻意加入的壓力條件，各角色實際運算量亦不同。

值得先讀角色設定與附錄的測試重分類，再看「問對、找對、修對」診斷。三十案例、單一模擬器、缺乏主要結果信賴區間，以及模型評判真實感的方式，都限制外推；搜尋種子答案的案例支持洩漏風險，但沒有隔離搜尋能力的隨機對照。全文四十五頁、四圖與二十一表已讀。這份基準適合研究模糊需求與長程協作失敗，尚不能把排行榜直接當成真實使用者成功率或普遍產品選購結論。

llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant adaptive-reasoning training method with a credible matched-control token/performance trade-off and a clear progressive labeling procedure. The strongest supported claim is lower generated reasoning-token use after benchmark-specific training, with reported success close to standard SFT+GRPO; statistical equivalence and total-compute savings are not established. Fixed-history teacher forcing and reference-action recovery do not measure all valid actions or off-trajectory robustness. Sequential local likelihood bounds can accumulate and do not prove a minimal or globally faithful reasoning cover. Missing threshold/order ablations, multi-seed uncertainty and measured labeling/training overhead limit rigor. The explicit AppWorld and small-model limitations are important. Complete supplied PDF and appendices were read; the linked repository and experimental results were not independently reproduced.

primary_link.title: When Should Agents Think? Adaptive Reasoning via Cross-Turn Estimation

top5.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks. They typically perform reasoning before each action throughout an interaction trajectory. However, reasoning may not be necessary at every turn, as reasoning produced earlier can continue to support subsequent actions. A key challenge is therefore to determine when existing reasoning remains sufficient and when a new reasoning step is needed, without relying on costly generation-based verification. We find that decreases in the likelihood of subsequent reference actions after removing additional reasoning closely track whether those actions remain recoverable given earlier reasoning, providing an effective and lightweight signal for estimating cross-turn action support. Based on this observation, we propose Reasoning Adaptation through Cross-Turn Estimation (RACE), a training approach for adaptive agent reasoning. RACE introduces a Likelihood-Guided Progressive Reasoning Cover Detection (LoGiC) procedure that progressively identifies reasoning turns whose removal has limited impact on the current and subsequent reference actions. The resulting removal signals are incorporated into both supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning, enabling the policy to learn when to reason and when to act directly. Extensive experiments on four representative agent benchmarks show that RACE substantially reduces reasoning cost while maintaining or improving task performance.
top5.summary_en: RACE learns when to omit agent reasoning using teacher-forced reference-action likelihood changes. Sequential removal labels guide SFT and GRPO masking plus reasoning-closure supervision. Against standard SFT+GRPO, the 9B policy cuts reasoning tokens by 32–80% with success differences within 1.4 points. Fixed-history action recovery is not a guarantee for free rollouts, and local thresholds do not bound cumulative drift. Missing uncertainty, threshold sensitivity and measured end-to-end compute limit stronger efficiency claims.
top5.summary_zh:
代理每次呼叫工具前都重新長篇思考，可能重複已經足夠的計畫。RACE 提出以既有行動的平均 token 對數似然，判斷某一回合的推理是否可省略。LoGiC 從第二回合起逐次嘗試移除推理，檢查目前及後續參考行動的似然下降是否都低於門檻，再把省略訊號用於監督微調，以及強化學習中的推理遮罩與結束標記監督。第一回合保留；部署時由訓練後策略決定思考或直接行動。

在九十億參數 Qwen 骨幹上，對照一般 SFT 加 GRPO，四項基準的推理 token 減少約三十二至八十％，成功率差距在一點四個百分點內；WebShop 為五十三點四％，對照五十二％，推理 token 從二千七百零二降至五百三十五。但這不是所有方法都被全面超越：AppWorld 成功率仍低於 AdaptThink，部分消融也以更多 token 換取較高成功率。

閱讀重點是省略訊號的邊界。分析保留原先行動與觀察，量測的是參考行動在固定歷史下能否重建，並非移除後自由執行必然成功。門檻限制每次移除的局部變化，也不保證相對原始軌跡的總下降。全文二十八頁提供公式、訓練參數、提示與案例，但缺隨機種子變異、信賴區間、門檻敏感度及實際訓練／端到端延遲比較；推理 token 節省不能直接當總運算或費用節省。它是值得追蹤的訓練方法，仍須更完整的效率與穩健性驗證。

evidence: PDF pp.2–5 Figures1–3, Sections2.2–2.6: JANUS maintains a nested intent stack, PRECIP folds completed-intent spans, PALIM recursively folds prefixes, and original records remain children in a recallable message tree. This is nonparametric context/memory adaptation, not weight training.

PDF pp.6,14–15 Tables1,5,6: task backbone DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash advertises1M context but Hippocam's configured W is128,000; HiAgent uses8,192. Single runs are explicit; auxiliary budgets and compute are unmatched, Letta disables reasoning and extraction settings/tool interfaces vary. StreamBench150 mean81.7 versus Letta81.3; Hippocam ScienceWorld81.9 versus ACE91.9.

PDF pp.7,15–16 Tables2,7: Frozen ScienceWorld78.9 versus ACE62.7/Plain48.8; sequential After–Fresh19.2pp, FEVER6.0pp. Alternative FEVER extraction reduces the latter to2pp. Frozen tasks restore source snapshots; sequential contrasts include ongoing target learning, and some baselines have narrower matched coverage. Target-cost tables exclude source-memory acquisition.

PDF pp.7–8,15–16 Figure5/Table3: GoodAI isolated85.1/interleaved88.7 uses protocols also differing in brief-answer requests, reset and wait handling; appendix expressly disallows attributing the increase to interleaving itself. LoCoMo covers10 conversations and scores77.6 versus A-Mem67.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro binary judging, not original lexical F1; the judge lacks the source conversation.

PDF pp.8–9,16–17 Tables4,8: MAB100 questions per length; Hippocam97/77/41 at6k/32k/64k, mean71.7. Removing recall on the same64k ingestion snapshot gives27 versus41. Main comparisons have different representations/budgets; some errors lose updates while others fail to use retained evidence.

PDF pp.9,17 Table4/A.4: without intent conditioning GoodAI interleaved falls88.7→65.6; two-sided paired sign-test p=.11. JANUS and intent boundaries remain, filler retention14→63%, and grading/answer behavior explain part of the gap. Prefix removal replaces old material with truncation and ToolBench300 accuracy falls78.7→65.7; episode-start19.7k versus50.7k is not total inference tokens.

PDF pp.9,17–18 Tables4,9: prefix-removal comparison uses Hippocam97.8%/9.62 actions, while separate knowledge-configuration comparison reports100%/8.12. These are separate reported comparisons and must not be merged into one universal baseline. Flat summary100%/9.68 and ACE playbook97.8%/9.00 do not establish general superiority to strategy induction; some held-out game files share task/room configurations.

PDF pp.18–20 Tables10–11/Figures6–8: ToolBench3086 item transitions from two chains use API-linked proxies; repeated transitions are not independent items.95.8% with no detected use remain unchanged. Four-word reuse is a weaker proxy, and ScienceWorld unchanged57.7 versus59.1 is small. Selected restaurant/recall lineages illustrate behavior without isolating causal mechanisms.

PDF pp.21–22 Figure9/Tables12–13: costs reprice recorded usage including auxiliary/memory calls, excluding judges, not invoices. ToolBench300 cost/correct .0159USD versus A-Mem .0260; DDXPlus .0097 versus .0091 favors A-Mem. Later intervals contain different tasks. Letta cached-input data missing, so no exact repriced cost assigned.

PDF p.22: ToolBench PALIM calls are34% of total cost and first subsequent calls10.8%, not a counterfactual net overhead. All methods share an API account with possible cross-run cache reuse. Hippocam's ToolBench cost advantage persists only while cached-input price is below roughly15% of a miss; reported schedule uses2%.

PDF pp.23–33 Algorithms1–2 and prompts: appendices specify intent replacement, pressure control, recall and role prompts with examples omitted. PALIM explicitly coarsens narrative but protects identifying details of extracted knowledge (pp.30–32), qualifying the main-text claim of general disuse fading. Main-agent prompts trust consolidated records while permitting new contradictory observations; memory-corruption robustness is not evaluated.

Complete PDF pp.1–33: references, all nine figures, thirteen tables and two algorithms read. No independently inspected own-system executable artifact or new experiment supports this review; task/sample manifests and cross-run uncertainty remain incomplete.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant and well-articulated memory architecture, with substantive appendix disclosure and breadth across memory and interactive tasks. Strong reported recall and ScienceWorld-transfer results justify attention, but unequal system budgets and interfaces plus single runs prevent clean attribution to the proposed mechanism. The use-and-disuse story must be narrowed: narrative coarsening is explicit, while extracted knowledge is instructed to retain its detail and95.8% of no-use transitions remain unchanged. Correlational reuse proxies, selected case lineages and sequential-task changes do not establish a causal forgetting or skill-learning law. The systems are not uniformly superior or cheaper, and quoted costs depend strongly on cache pricing and exclude some acquisition/evaluation costs. Complete source reading supports a provisional full-text assessment, not reproduction, comprehensive lifetime reliability or general safety of persistent memory.

primary_link.title: Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents

top5.summary: The evolution of Large Language Model agents from single-task execution to long-term autonomous operation highlights the critical challenge of transforming continuous experiences into reusable knowledge. To address this, we propose Hippocam, a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture. Hippocam draws inspiration from two characteristics of human memory: cognitive processes selectively maintain information relevant to current goals, while long-term memories form gradually through repeated consolidation. Accordingly, Hippocam structures an agent's ongoing work as nested intents. The active context remains centered on the current intent, while completed intents are consolidated into the task-relevant outcomes and state needed for subsequent work, rather than carrying forward their full working details. Concurrently, a recursive prefix consolidation mechanism repeatedly consolidates earlier history, causing long-unused experiences to become increasingly abstract. Original interactions are preserved, allowing the agent to progressively recover finer-grained details through the hierarchy and stop once sufficient information is available. Crucially, when past experiences are recalled and reintegrated into active work, they undergo subsequent consolidation alongside new experiences, thereby being reinforced, supplemented, and updated. Through this memory dynamic of use and disuse, Hippocam connects working context, long-term memory, knowledge accumulation, and skill learning within a single continuously evolving experiential process. This enables agents to learn and evolve capabilities through their own experiences without parameter updates.
top5.summary_en: Hippocam turns intent-guided context consolidation and a recoverable message tree into nonparametric agent memory. It reports broad single-run gains, including LoCoMo 77.6% versus A-Mem 67.5%, but does not win every task. Compute, context budgets, reasoning modes and interfaces differ across systems. Its use-and-disuse analysis is associative: 95.8% of unused-item transitions stay unchanged, and prompts protect extracted knowledge. Cache-sensitive costs and limited uncertainty constrain general learning claims.
top5.summary_zh:
Hippocam 嘗試把代理的工作紀錄同時作為短期上下文、長期記憶與經驗學習來源。JANUS 管理巢狀意圖與完成條件；PRECIP 在意圖結束時留下結果、證據及仍有用途的細節；PALIM 則反覆整合較早前綴。原始訊息保存在樹狀檔案中，代理可逐層回憶，取得足夠證據後停止，而不必一次展開整段歷史。這是非參數式經驗更新，沒有訓練模型權重。

在同一 DeepSeek 骨幹的多種任務中，方法呈現較廣的能力組合：LoCoMo 模型判定正確率為七十七點六％，高於 A-Mem 的六十七點五％；六十四千 token 量級的 MAB 輸入則由不開回憶的二十七％提升至四十一％。但 ScienceWorld 仍低於 ACE，StreamBench 前一百五十題平均也只領先 Letta 零點四個百分點。

必讀附錄的限制：所有設定僅跑一次，總推論量、記憶預算、推理模式及工具介面未對齊；GoodAI 兩模式亦有其他差異，不能把增益全部歸因於意圖或交錯任務。所謂用進廢退的分析多為相關性，九十五點八％未偵測到使用的知識轉換仍維持原樣，提示詞還要求保留已抽取知識。成本優勢依賴快取折扣，並非普遍較省。完整三十三頁及圖表支持有用的記憶架構提案，尚不足以證明一般終身學習或因果式遺忘機制。
